tools.name: find_tool
tools.description: Search available MCP tools by keyword or category before calling them. Returns matching tool names, descriptions, and optionally their inputSchemas. Call this when you are unsure which tool to use or want to explore the catalogue. Categories: data, encoding, text, llm, qa, rag, dev, security, web.

tools.name: prompt_injection_scan
tools.description: Scan user input or prompts for common prompt injection patterns. Pattern-based: it recognises known phrasings and structural markers, not intent — a paraphrase it has no pattern for, or a language it does not cover, reads clean, so a clean result is not proof of safety. The instruction-override phra

tools.name: guardrail_test
tools.description: Test an LLM response against a set of guardrail rules: must-include, must-not-include, max length, required format, language, forbidden patterns, and custom regex. Returns pass/fail per rule.

tools.name: redact_pii
tools.description: Automatically detect and redact Personally Identifiable Information (PII) from text. Replaces emails, phone numbers, SSNs, IBANs, credit cards, IP addresses, and JWT tokens with [REDACTED_TYPE] placeholders. Safe to use before logging or sending to an LLM.

tools.name: secret_scan
tools.description: Scan text or code for leaked secrets: API keys (AWS, GCP, Azure, OpenAI, Anthropic, Stripe, GitHub, GitLab, Slack, Twilio, SendGrid, HuggingFace), private keys (RSA/EC/PGP), JWTs, database connection strings, Bearer tokens, and Basic auth headers. Returns a list of findings with type, severity, line

tools.name: validate_agent_trajectory
tools.description: Run declarative assertions on an agent trace (OpenAI tool-call messages, Anthropic tool_use/tool_result blocks, LangChain run trees, or plain text ReAct logs). No LLM call — deterministic. Assertion types: order (tool A before B), must_call, must_not_call, max_calls, min_calls, no_error, recovery (a

tools.name: validate_mcp_response
tools.description: Validate that an MCP tool response conforms to expected format, schema, and content rules. Use this to QA-test any MCP server tool. Supply the tool's actual JSON result and a set of checks to perform.

tools.name: mcp_server_health_check
tools.description: Check an MCP server's tool definitions without contacting it — for a server not deployed yet, a stdio server, or a CI gate. Paste the answer to tools/list (raw JSON-RPC or its result), a bare array of tools, one tool definition, or a manifest carrying name/description; input_shape says which one was

tools.name: mcp_server_evaluate
tools.description: Run a compliance evaluation against a live MCP server over Streamable HTTP, the way a client meets it. Checks: initialize (protocol version, serverInfo, Mcp-Session-Id carried afterwards), notifications/initialized (202), tools/list with pagination, the spec's tool-definition rules, ping, an unknown

tools.name: toxicity_scan
tools.description: Scan text for toxic language, hate speech, bias/stereotype framing, violence, sexual and self-harm content. Lexical + structural pattern matching (identity term + predicate), not a semantic classifier — returns per-category risk plus the named rules that fired, so every finding can be checked. Langu

tools.name: function_call_validate
tools.description: Validate an LLM function call / tool_use output: check that function name is in allowed list, arguments match expected schema (types, enums, ranges), no extra/missing args. Reads the definitions as OpenAI (`parameters`), MCP (`inputSchema`) or Anthropic (`input_schema`) write them, or as plain `requ

tools.name: mcp_schema_lint
tools.description: Lint an MCP tool definition for best practices: naming conventions, description quality, schema completeness, required fields consistency, description length. Returns actionable warnings.

tools.name: bias_detect
tools.description: Analyse a set of LLM responses generated from the same prompt template but with different demographic variants (gender, origin, age, tone). Returns a bias score (0-100), sentiment analysis per variant, pairwise Jaccard similarity, and a human-readable verdict. No API key needed — runs entirely local

tools.name: shield_analyze
tools.description: Run a comprehensive AI guardrail analysis on an LLM response. Orchestrates 7 deterministic safety checks plus an optional LLM-powered deep analysis in parallel: hallucination detection (grounding score), prompt injection scan on BOTH the response and the original prompt (reported separately as check

tools.name: security_headers_check
tools.description: Analyse the HTTP security headers of a public URL OR of raw response headers you paste in. Grades each header (A–F) for: Strict-Transport-Security, Content-Security-Policy, X-Frame-Options, X-Content-Type-Options, Referrer-Policy, Permissions-Policy, X-XSS-Protection, Cross-Origin-Opener-Policy, Cro

tools.name: ssl_certificate_check
tools.description: Analyse the SSL/TLS certificate of any HTTPS host. Returns certificate subject, issuer, validity dates, days until expiry, protocol version, cipher suite, key exchange info, and an overall grade (A+, A, B, C, F). Detects expired, self-signed, and weak certificates. Use this to audit TLS posture befo

tools.name: cors_test
tools.description: Test a URL for CORS misconfigurations. Sends preflight (OPTIONS) requests with various Origin headers to detect: wildcard origins with credentials, origin reflection (echoing any origin), null origin acceptance, subdomain wildcard bypass, and missing Vary headers. Returns risk level (safe/low/medium

tools.name: cors_checker
tools.description: Check the CORS configuration of a URL the same way a browser would. Returns the main response status, all Access-Control-* headers, the tested origin, and the preflight OPTIONS response. Use this for direct CORS debugging, not just security auditing.

tools.name: cookie_security_audit
tools.description: Audit the security attributes of cookies set by any URL. Fetches the URL and inspects all Set-Cookie headers for: HttpOnly, Secure, SameSite, Domain scope, Path scope, Max-Age/Expires, __Host-/__Secure- prefixes. Flags insecure patterns: missing HttpOnly on session cookies, missing Secure flag, Same

tools.name: web_security_audit
tools.description: Run a comprehensive web security audit combining headers, SSL, CORS, and cookies checks — then use an LLM to produce a prioritised remediation plan. Orchestrates security_headers_check + ssl_certificate_check + cors_test + cookie_security_audit in parallel, merges all findings, then asks an AI model

tools.name: rate_tool
tools.description: Give honest usage feedback on an IA-QA MCP tool. Provide a score (1-5) and a comment. Rate low (1-2) if the tool was wrong, irrelevant, or a poor fit; rate high (4-5) only if it genuinely solved your need. Ratings are read by the IA-QA maintainers and are not published, one vote per agent and tool a

tools.name: decode_jwt
tools.description: Decode a JWT (JSON Web Token) and return its header and payload without verifying the signature. Also reports whether the token is expired and the exact expiry date. Use to inspect claims (sub, iss, exp, roles) during debugging or when integrating with an auth provider.

tools.name: validate_url
tools.description: Parse and validate a URL. Returns decomposed components: protocol, hostname, port, path, query parameters, hash, and origin.

tools.name: http_status_lookup
tools.description: Look up detailed information about any HTTP status code: class, name, description, cacheability, typical causes, and handling best practices. Covers every code in the IANA HTTP Status Code Registry (1xx-5xx, including 226, 425, 451, 508, 511 and the WebDAV codes) with its defining RFC; anything outs

tools.name: parse_http_headers
tools.description: Parse a raw HTTP headers block into a structured JSON object. Detects multi-value headers, masks Authorization values, and optionally audits for missing security headers (HSTS, CSP, X-Frame-Options, etc.).

tools.name: detect_secrets
tools.description: Scan code or config files for hardcoded secrets: AWS keys, GitHub tokens, OpenAI/Anthropic API keys, Stripe secrets, JWTs, database connection strings, and generic passwords. Returns findings with severity. Run before every commit.

tools.name: latency_benchmark
tools.description: Measure response time of one or more HTTP endpoints (GET/POST). Runs N iterations and returns min/max/avg/p95 latency. Useful for API and MCP server benchmarking.

tools.name: hash_text
tools.description: Compute a cryptographic hash of a text string. Use when you need to verify data integrity, generate content fingerprints, hash passwords (prefer SHA-256+), or produce a fixed-length digest of any input. Supports SHA-256 (default), SHA-512, SHA-1, and MD5.

tools.name: generate_password
tools.description: Generate a cryptographically secure random password using crypto.randomBytes. Configurable length (4–128), uppercase letters, digits, and symbols. Use when resetting user passwords, seeding test accounts, or generating API secrets.

tools.name: generate_hmac
tools.description: Compute an HMAC signature for a message using a secret key. Supports SHA-256 (default), SHA-512, SHA-1, and MD5. Used for API request signing, webhook verification (GitHub, Stripe, Twilio), and JWT validation.

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "security" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: validate_agent_trajectory, mcp_server_evaluate, shield_analyze, security_headers_check, ssl_certificate_check, cors_test, cors_checker, rate_tool, latency_benchmark · Private data: prompt_injection_scan, redact_pii, secret_scan, mcp_server_evaluate, bias_detect, security_headers_check, cors_test, rate_tool, decode_jwt, detect_secrets, hash_text, generate_password, generate_hmac · Public sink: mcp_server_evaluate, shield_analyze, latency_benchmark, generate_hmac · Destructive: guardrail_test, validate_agent_trajectory, validate_mcp_response, mcp_server_evaluate, shield_analyze, web_security_audit, detect_secrets.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: validate_agent_trajectory, mcp_server_evaluate, shield_analyze, security_headers_check, ssl_certificate_check, cors_test, cors_checker, rate_tool, latency_benchmark · Private data: prompt_injection_scan, redact_pii, secret_scan, mcp_server_evaluate, bias_detect, security_headers_check, cors_test, rate_tool, decode_jwt, detect_secrets, hash_text, generate_password, generate_hmac · Public sink: mcp_server_evaluate, shield_analyze, latency_benchmark, generate_hmac · Destructive: guardrail_test, validate_agent_trajectory, validate_mcp_response, mcp_server_evaluate, shield_analyze, web_security_audit, detect_secrets

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.

findings.detail: Tool "prompt_injection_scan" changed its description with no version change. Silent description changes are how a trusted server turns malicious after review.

Pattern-based: it recognises known phrasings and structural markers, not intent — a paraphrase it has no pattern for, or a language it does not cover, reads clean, so a clean result is not proof of safety. The instruction-override phra"

findings.remediation: Re-review the tool before continuing to trust it.
